name: Jhenaidah
tagline: Mughal-era mosques scattered through Barobazar, the largest banyan in Bangladesh, and the village where a 19-year-old Bir Sreshtho was born.

guide.bestTime: October to March — cool, dry, easy on the road. Avoid peak monsoon for the rural mosques on dirt approaches.
guide.gettingThere: By road from Dhaka (~190 km, ~5 hr) via the Dhaka–Khulna highway or via Magura. By rail, alight at Kotchandpur or Mobarakganj on the Khulna line, or at Darshana / Chuadanga and CNG in. The mosques cluster at Barobazar in Kaliganj; Hamidnagar and Dattanagar lie in Mohespur, far southwest.
guide.difficulty: Easy — town and Kaliganj sights are short hops by CNG; only Hamidnagar / Mohespur is a longer drive.

mustVisit.name: Galakata Mosque (Barobazar)
mustVisit.description: A single-domed brick mosque from the Sultanate period — squat, severe and beautifully detailed, with two free-standing stone columns of clearly older Hindu temple origin inside, repurposed as supports.
mustVisit.history: Built in the late 15th–early 16th century at the Sultanate-era settlement of Barobazar, one of more than a dozen old mosques scattered around the bazar. Excavated and protected by the Department of Archaeology.

practical.hours: Daylight hours; mosque opens around prayer times

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 30 km southeast of Jhenaidah town in Barobazar Union of Kaliganj Upazila
howToReach.transport: Bus / CNG to Barobazar, then short walk

mustVisit.bestTime: Late afternoon for the brickwork light
tips: Combine with Jor Bangla and other Barobazar mosques on the same trip
Cover head if female; remove shoes before entering
The two stone columns inside are the rare bit — don't miss them

mustVisit.name: Jor Bangla Mosque
mustVisit.description: A small Sultanate-era mosque at Barobazar with a curved-cornice 'do-chala' roofline borrowed from village Bengali architecture — a rare survivor where Hindu thatched-hut form was lifted whole into Muslim sacred building.
mustVisit.history: Late 15th–16th century brick mosque in Barobazar, part of the same Sultanate settlement as Galakata. The 'jor bangla' (twin-hut) form is one of the early hybrid Bengali styles of mosque architecture.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 30 km southeast of Jhenaidah town in Barobazar, Kaliganj
howToReach.transport: Bus / CNG to Barobazar, easy walk between mosques

mustVisit.bestTime: Morning light through the surrounding fields
tips: Walk between the cluster of Barobazar mosques — at least a dozen Sultanate-era survivors
Bring water; the bazar is small, refreshments thin

mustVisit.name: Naldanga Rajbari
mustVisit.description: The ruined palace of the Naldanga zamindar family, set among gardens and temples on the bank of the Chitra river — Doric pillars, broken pediments and the quiet of a feudal estate gone to seed.
mustVisit.history: Seat of one of Bengal's oldest Hindu zamindar lines, the Naldanga Raj, said to date from the 12th–13th centuries; the present brick complex was built mainly in the 18th–19th centuries and includes temples to Shiva, Vishnu and Govinda alongside the main rajbari.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 30 km west of Jhenaidah town in Kaliganj Upazila, on the Chitra river
howToReach.transport: Bus / CNG to Kaliganj, then local rickshaw to Naldanga

tips: Mind your step — sections of the rajbari are unstable
Look for the Govinda temple's terracotta panels behind the main building

mustVisit.name: Mallikpur Banyan Tree (Suitala)
mustVisit.description: A roughly 300-year-old banyan that has spread over more than two acres of village land — dozens of aerial roots have grown into trunks, the canopy walks itself out into a forest of its own.
mustVisit.history: Locally called Suitala Bot, at Mallikpur village in Kaliganj. Reckoned by Bangladesh tree counts as the largest banyan in the country and one of the largest in Asia; the Forest Department has been working to stabilise its declining limbs.

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 25 km southeast of Jhenaidah town, in Kaliganj Upazila on the Kaliganj–Khajura road
howToReach.transport: Bus / CNG to Kaliganj, then rickshaw or van to Mallikpur

mustVisit.bestTime: Cool months; afternoon light filters through the aerial roots
tips: Don't pull on the aerial roots — many are still alive and load-bearing
Pair with Naldanga Rajbari on the same day — same upazila

mustVisit.name: Birsreshtho Hamidur Rahman Memorial (Hamidnagar)
mustVisit.description: The birthplace village of Bir Sreshtho Mohammad Hamidur Rahman — a small museum, school and memorial in the village now renamed Hamidnagar in his honour, on the Indian border.
mustVisit.history: Hamidur Rahman was born here in February 1953 in what was then Khordo Khalishpur village of Mohespur thana. He died at Dhalai in Moulvibazar on 28 October 1971, silencing a Pakistan Army machine-gun in hand-to-hand combat; he was posthumously awarded the Bir Sreshtho.

practical.hours: Daylight hours; ask at the village school office

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 60 km southwest of Jhenaidah town in Mohespur Upazila, near the Indian border
howToReach.transport: Bus to Mohespur, then CNG to Hamidnagar

tips: The border is patrolled — carry ID
Combine with Dattanagar Agricultural Farm, a short drive away

mustVisit.name: Dattanagar Agricultural Farm
mustVisit.description: A 3,000-acre seed farm — for decades described as the largest seed-production farm in Asia. Endless flat fields of paddy, jute, oilseed and pulse trials, with the Indian border one canal across.
mustVisit.history: Established by the Pakistan government in the 1960s as a seed-multiplication centre, the Dattanagar Agricultural Farm in Mohespur covers about 3,000 acres and produces foundation seed for distribution across the country's farms.

practical.hours: Working hours, weekdays; visits by request

howToReach.fromDistrictTown: About 65 km southwest of Jhenaidah town in Mohespur Upazila
howToReach.transport: Bus to Mohespur, then CNG to Dattanagar

mustVisit.bestTime: Sowing season (post-monsoon) or harvest — fields are at their fullest
tips: Ask permission at the farm office before walking the plots
The border canal runs along one edge — stay on the Bangladeshi side

specialties.name: Nalen Gurer Sandesh
specialties.description: Date-palm jaggery sandesh — Jhenaidah and the Jashore region together are one of the country's great date-palm belts. The winter pitha and sandesh stalls along the highway are reason enough to drive through.
specialties.venue: Highway sweet stalls and town confectioners (winter)

specialties.name: Kaliganj Pottery
specialties.description: Generations of potters in Kaliganj turn out terracotta water pots, ritual lamps and figures — a craft town tucked behind the Mughal mosques.

bucketlist.title: Walk the Sultanate mosques of Barobazar
bucketlist.detail: More than a dozen 15th–16th-century brick mosques scattered through one country market town — Galakata, Jor Bangla, Sukur Mallick, Goragor — a quiet archaeological landscape.

bucketlist.title: Find the temple-pillars inside Galakata Mosque
bucketlist.detail: Two stone columns inside the single-domed brick mosque — repurposed from an older Hindu temple, one of the clearest signs in Bangladesh of a Sultanate-era cultural cross-over.

bucketlist.title: Wander Naldanga Rajbari at golden hour
bucketlist.detail: Broken pediments, garden temples and the Chitra river behind — the seat of one of Bengal's oldest Hindu zamindar lines, said to date from the 12th–13th centuries.

bucketlist.title: Stand inside Bangladesh's biggest banyan
bucketlist.detail: Three centuries of growth at Suitala, Mallikpur — the canopy walks itself outward on hundreds of aerial roots, more like a small forest than a single tree.

bucketlist.title: Visit Bir Sreshtho Hamidur Rahman's village
bucketlist.detail: The renamed village of Hamidnagar in Mohespur — a small museum, school and memorial at the birthplace of the 19-year-old sepoy who silenced a machine-gun at Dhalai in 1971.

bucketlist.title: See the Dattanagar seed fields
bucketlist.detail: Three thousand acres of foundation-seed plots — paddy, jute, oilseed, pulse — long described as the largest seed farm in Asia, with the Indian border one canal across.

bucketlist.title: Buy nalen gur at a roadside stall in winter
bucketlist.detail: The Jashore–Jhenaidah belt is one of Bangladesh's great date-palm regions; the winter pitha and sandesh stalls along the highway pour fresh khejurer gur on everything.

bucketlist.title: Take a boat on the Chitra river
bucketlist.detail: The Chitra threads past Naldanga, Kaliganj town and a string of old ghats and temples — a slow, half-day country boat ride at the right level.

bucketlist.title: Visit a Kaliganj potter's village
bucketlist.detail: Generations of terracotta pot-makers — water jars, ritual lamps, votive figures — a quiet craft town tucked behind the Mughal mosques.

bucketlist.title: Track down Kavi Golam Mostafa's Manoharpur
bucketlist.detail: Sailkupa's most famous son — the poet who wrote 'Biswanabi' was born in Manoharpur, in a family of Qazis fluent in Bengali, Arabic and Persian.

foods.name: Nalen Gurer Sandesh
foods.description: Sandesh made with fresh winter date-palm jaggery — Jhenaidah and Jashore together are one of the country's great khejurer-gur belts.
foods.whereToFind: Highway sweet stalls and town confectioners (winter)

foods.name: Pitha (Bhapa, Patishapta, Chitoi)
foods.description: Winter rice-flour cakes — bhapa with gur and coconut, patishapta filled with kheer, chitoi dipped in date-palm syrup.

foods.name: Khejurer Ras
foods.description: Fresh date-palm sap collected from the trees at dawn — drunk lightly chilled on a cold morning before the sun ferments it.
foods.whereToFind: Date-palm villages around Kaliganj, Sailkupa, Mohespur (winter)

famousPeople.name: Bir Sreshtho Mohammad Hamidur Rahman
famousPeople.knownFor: Sepoy of the Bangladesh Forces who silenced a Pakistan Army machine-gun in hand-to-hand combat at Dhalai (Moulvibazar) on 28 October 1971 and was killed in the action — posthumously awarded the Bir Sreshtho. Born in Khordo Khalishpur village of Mohespur, Jhenaidah, now renamed Hamidnagar in his honour.

famousPeople.name: Kavi Golam Mostafa
famousPeople.knownFor: Poet, biographer and translator whose Biswanabi (1942), a Bengali biography of the Prophet Muhammad, became a defining work of Muslim Bengali letters. Born in 1897 at Manoharpur village in Sailkupa, in a Qazi family fluent in Bengali, Arabic and Persian.

didYouKnow: Bir Sreshtho Mohammad Hamidur Rahman — one of only seven recipients of Bangladesh's highest gallantry honour — was born in Khordo Khalishpur village of Mohespur, Jhenaidah, in 1953; the village has since been renamed Hamidnagar.
The Mallikpur (Suitala) banyan tree in Kaliganj has spread over two acres of village land in roughly three centuries — reckoned the largest banyan in Bangladesh.
Barobazar in Kaliganj is one of the densest clusters of Sultanate-era mosques in the country — more than a dozen 15th–16th-century brick mosques survive within a few kilometres.
Dattanagar Agricultural Farm in Mohespur covers about 3,000 acres and has long been described as the largest seed-multiplication farm in Asia.
Kavi Golam Mostafa, author of the 1942 Bengali biography Biswanabi, was born in Manoharpur village of Sailkupa, Jhenaidah, in 1897.
Naldanga, on the Chitra river, was seat of one of Bengal's oldest Hindu zamindar families — the Naldanga Raj is traced back to the 12th–13th centuries.
